title: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound
summary: There are absolute constants $`\eta,c_1\gt 0`$ such that, for every sufficiently large integer n , one can choose n points in the unit square so that every triangle they determine has area at least $`c_1n^{-2+\eta}`$. Thus the almost n −2 upper-bound formulation of Heilbronn's triangle problem is false. The exponent η is fixed but extremely small.
